children: Micron Technology
extended its recent slide Tuesday, falling another
roughly 4%
as concerns around Chinese competition, memory-chip pricing and the broader AI trade continued to pressure semiconductor stocks.
Micron closed at
, down $35.85 from the previous session, according to Seeking Alpha. The decline added to a recent stretch of weakness even as the company moves ahead with a record
$35.16 billion share-buyback program
The latest pressure is increasingly tied to China.
ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, has unveiled progress on a denser DRAM architecture known as
4F

and plans to launch a new DDR5 server-memory product by the end of 2026. The announcement has raised fears that Chinese capacity could eventually add more supply to a memory market where tight conditions have supported pricing and margins.

Elon Musk also added to the concern, pointing to China's ability to scale memory production rapidly. While he noted that high-bandwidth memory remains a harder technological challenge for Chinese suppliers, investors are clearly becoming more sensitive to any sign that conventional DRAM competition is increasing.
The weakness is not isolated to Micron.

Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix also suffered sharp declines as a broader semiconductor selloff spread across Asia and the U.S. Reuters described the session as part of a wider repricing of AI-linked stocks amid concerns over valuations, financing costs and whether huge infrastructure investments can deliver adequate returns.
Investor Takeaway
I think the important distinction is that
Micron's long-term AI memory thesis has not necessarily broken, but investors are starting to price in more cyclical risk

Micron remains highly exposed to HBM and advanced DRAM demand from AI servers, where supply remains constrained. But conventional DRAM still represents a large part of its business, making Chinese capacity expansion relevant even if CXMT cannot immediately compete at the cutting edge.
The selloff is also occurring after an enormous rally, which makes the stock more vulnerable to any sign of future oversupply or margin normalization.
For investors, the key things to watch are
HBM pricing, DRAM contract prices, CXMT production ramp, memory inventories and whether AI infrastructure spending continues at the current pace

If Chinese supply remains limited and HBM stays tight, the recent weakness could prove largely sentiment-driven. If CXMT scales faster than expected, however, the market may begin assigning a lower multiple to Micron well before actual pricing pressure appears.

title: Micron Takes Another Hit as China Chip Fears Flare
